text:
maria: Heads-up — brought up krypton20b (int4) in canary this morning. Good perf on short prompts but we hit sporadic OOMs on some long-chat workloads and a small quality delta vs float16 baseline.
kevin: paste logs? which workloads and config?
maria: attaching quick repro from canary run: \n```
model: krypton20b
quant: int4
batch_size: 8
max_new_tokens: 512
kv_prefetch: true
slot_reserve: 0.06
packing_window: 128
compactor: enabled
```
error snippet: \n"CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 48.00 GiB total capacity; 43.1 GiB already allocated)"

ajay: ok likely fragmentation + large max_new_tokens. we've seen int4 can spike with long kv life. can you repro with max_new_tokens=128 and packing_window=64?
kevin: also try lowering slot_reserve to 0.02 or enable early-kv-evict=false to see if evictions are thrashing.
maria: ran quick variants: \n- v1 (canary): max_new_tokens=512, batch=8 -> intermittent OOMs (1/25 runs)
- v2: max_new_tokens=128, batch=8 -> no OOMs, p50 latency +5%
- v3: max_new_tokens=512, batch=4 -> fewer OOMs but still saw a failure

jun: interesting — perf hit when you lower max_new_tokens, but stability wins. what about quality for v2 vs float16? any eval diffs?
ci-bot: autop-run results:\n- float16 baseline ROUGE-L on summarization set: 43.7
- int4 v1 (512): 42.1
- int4 v2 (128): 42.8
- delta(float16 -> int4 v2): -0.9
- throughput (tokens/s): float16 2900, int4 v2 3700

ajay: quality gap shrank when we limit generation length — likely tokenization/quant jitter on long tails. Could do a hybrid default: max_new_tokens default 128 for public canary, and offer explicit higher-max param for advanced users.
kevin: ops note: we should also instrument KV cache lifetime + slab fragmentation. propose adding a short GC pass after request completion for int4 canary hosts (compact-slot-on-idle true) and rerun the canary.
maria: did that: compact-slot-on-idle=true + max_new_tokens=256 + batch=6 -> no OOMs, p50 latency +8%, rouge-L 42.6. seems like sweet spot.
jun: try one more: enable tensor-swap to host for coldest tensors (swap_threshold=0.4) — might reduce fragmentation at cost of tail latency.
maria: queued a sweep overnight with tensor-swap on and int8 mixed-precision option as fallback. results will be in the canary dashboard tomorrow.
kevin: plan for immediate action:\n1) rollback canary v1 traffic -> stop exposing 512 default
2) set org default max_new_tokens=128 for krypton20b int4
3) enable compact-slot-on-idle on canary int4 hosts
4) run eval sweep (summarize+qa) comparing int4(128) vs float16 and int8-fallback

ajay: +1. we should also add a targeted test in our CI that simulates long-chat with many short messages to catch frag regressions earlier.
ci-bot: created ticket INF-7842 with the canary logs and sweep configs. CI test added to experimental-onboard suite.
maria: thanks team. will follow up with numbers tomorrow and propose a rollout plan if overnight sweep is stable. :thumbsup:\n
